summary.intent: Implement GitHub issue #618 (cipher-box core: strict deterministic-CBOR codec, error surface, and KAT test infrastructure) while parallelizing other independent v2-build slices (#624 API auth, #623 engine scaffold, #645 desktop Tauri shell) via background worktree agents.
summary.outcome: #618 was fully implemented, verified (native + wasm32-wasip1, clippy/fmt, KAT generator determinism, workspace tests), and committed: codec module, two-class error surface, 72 KAT vectors, 11 manifest tests, 5 proptest properties, and a new CI job. Four additional slices (#624, #623, #645, plus the proptest/KAT sub-agents) were kicked off or completed in parallel worktrees.

repo: cipher-box v2-build issues declare explicit 'Depends on:' lines in their bodies, usable to find issues safe to parallelize

crates/engine has a placeholder cross-crate test that references cipherbox_core::CRATE — any core API change requires updating it, and it's a recurring collision point between core-touching and engine-touching branches
CI changes to ci.yml require running actionlint and zizmor locally before commit, plus validating YAML syntax
New CI job names must land via an actual PR run before branch protection required-checks can be registered against them
wasm testing uses wasm32-wasip1 target run under wasmtime; native fs (include_str! is fine, runtime fs reads are not) must be avoided in tests destined for wasm

code.finding: Half-float bit patterns could alias simple-value encodings (f90014 was indistinguishable from `false`) — decode dispatch must key on additional-info, not just major type, to avoid this class of bug. Caught during self-review before merge.

Vec<&'static str>::contains(&k) can't accept the HRTB &str closure arg needed in decode_map_partial; clippy's manual_contains suggestion (contains(&k)) would not compile — had to use BTreeSet<&str> instead.
proptest's default 'fork' feature (pulls in wait-timeout) fails to build under wasm32-wasip1; needed a target-conditional dev-dependency split (forkless proptest on wasm).
Placeholder cross-crate test asserted against cipherbox_core::CRATE, which was removed when the real codec/error API landed; swapped to exercise the actual codec surface.

workflow: Launching independent GitHub issues as background worktree agents in parallel is effective, but architecture-defining slices (e.g. engine seam traits) should be flagged for human review before merge rather than auto-merged
Issues requiring physical hardware/environment setup (e.g. FUSE-T, real SMB mounts) are unsuitable for background agents and should be left for interactive sessions
Splitting proptest dev-dependency by target (forkless on wasm) resolves proptest's 'fork' feature (wait-timeout) failing to build under wasm32-wasip1

friction: proptest's fork feature broke the wasm32-wasip1 build, requiring a target-specific dev-dependency workaround
Half-float/simple-value bit-pattern aliasing was a subtle decoder bug only caught via self-review, not initial tests
Clippy's own suggested fix (manual_contains) for the HRTB Vec::contains issue didn't actually compile, requiring a different data structure (BTreeSet)
Known merge conflict seeded between the #618 and #623 branches on crates/engine/src/lib.rs (placeholder test), deferred as a 'trivial rebase' for whichever merges second
open_items: #623 engine scaffold (architecture-defining seam traits/fakes/facade) requires human review before merge
#644 desktop hardware verification gates deferred to an interactive session (needs FUSE-T installed and real SMB mounts)
Branch protection required-checks entry for the new 'Core KATs (native + WASM)' CI job still needs to be registered once a PR run proves the job name
#618 branch committed locally but PR not yet opened/reviewed as of end of transcript
Expected trivial rebase conflict on crates/engine/src/lib.rs between #618 and #623 branches, whichever merges second
